detailedDescription: Automatically stash uncommitted changes when switching branches. When enabled, Kunj will save your work-in-progress before switching and restore it when you return to the branch. This prevents losing uncommitted changes when moving between branches.
examples: false - Never stash, require clean working tree

detailedDescription: Determines how branches are sorted in lists and menus. "recent" sorts by last activity (most recently used first), while "alphabetical" sorts branches by name in A-Z order.
examples: recent - Show most recently used branches first

detailedDescription: Number of items to display per page in interactive menus. Larger values show more items at once but may be harder to navigate. Smaller values require more scrolling but are easier to scan.
Use Unicode box-drawing characters (│ ├ ─ ╮ ╯ ●) instead of ASCII (* | / \) in commit graphs. Unicode provides a more polished, continuous look but may not render correctly in all terminals.
examples: true - Use Unicode characters for prettier graphs
false - Use ASCII characters for compatibility (default)

detailedDescription: Color scheme for commit graphs. Choose based on your terminal background: "default" for balanced colors, "light" optimized for light backgrounds with darker colors, "dark" optimized for dark backgrounds with brighter colors.
examples: light - Optimized for light terminal backgrounds
dark - Optimized for dark terminal backgrounds

description: Default base branch for new branches and PRs
detailedDescription: The branch new branches are created from (kunj create, switch -c, worktree add -b/-c) and that pull requests target. Common values are "main", "master", or "develop". If not set, the repository default (origin/HEAD, else main or master) is used. --base overrides it for one command.
examples: main - Use main as the default base branch
master - Use master as the default base branch
develop - Use develop as the default base branch

detailedDescription: Fetch the base branch from origin and create new branches from origin/<base> rather than the local copy, so they start from the latest remote commit. Falls back to the local branch when the repository has no origin or the branch is not on it. --no-origin turns it off for one command. New branches never track the base; push them with -u as usual.
examples: true - Fetch and branch from origin/<base> (default)
false - Branch from the local <base> without fetching

description: Small/cheap model for bulk operations (e.g. map phase in team reports)

detailedDescription: Choose the format for AI-generated commit messages and PR descriptions. Each style follows different conventions for organizing and presenting changes. This applies to both commit messages and pull request descriptions.
examples: custom - Use customInstructions for your own format

detailedDescription: Additional instructions for the AI to follow when generating commit messages and PR descriptions. Use this to enforce team conventions, add specific requirements, or customize the output format. These instructions are added to all AI prompts.
examples: "Focus on business value over technical details"

detailedDescription: When enabled, AI automatically generates pull request titles and descriptions when you run "kunj pr". The AI analyzes code changes, commit history, and branch metadata to create comprehensive PR descriptions. Falls back to heuristic generation if AI fails.
examples: true - Use AI for PR descriptions (recommended)

description: Include full diff for PR context
detailedDescription: When generating PR descriptions, include the full code diff for AI analysis. This provides better context and more accurate descriptions, but may be slower for large changes. If disabled, the AI only uses commit messages and branch metadata.
examples: true - Analyze full code changes (better quality)

detailedDescription: Enable Git Flow branching model in this repository. When enabled, you can use the `kunj flow` command to manage feature, release, and hotfix branches following the Git Flow methodology.
The main production branch where stable releases are maintained. This is typically "main" or "master". Release and hotfix branches will be merged into this branch.
examples: main - Use main as production branch (default)
master - Use master as production branch

detailedDescription: The integration branch for ongoing development. Feature branches are created from and merged back into this branch. This is typically "develop" or "dev".
examples: develop - Use develop as integration branch (default)
dev - Use dev as integration branch
development - Use development as integration branch

detailedDescription: Prefix for feature branch names. Feature branches are created for new features and improvements. Use empty string for no prefix.
Prefix for release branch names. Release branches are created to prepare new production releases. Use empty string for no prefix.
Prefix for hotfix branch names. Hotfix branches are created from production to quickly patch critical bugs. Use empty string for no prefix.
Automatically delete feature/release/hotfix branches after successfully finishing them. When disabled, you will be prompted to confirm deletion for each branch.
examples: true - Automatically delete branches after merge (default)
false - Always ask before deleting branches

description: Git Flow mode: local or pr
detailedDescription: Choose how Git Flow operations are performed. "local" uses local git merges, while "pr" creates and merges pull requests on your remote provider (GitHub, GitLab, etc.).
examples: pr - Use pull requests on remote provider

detailedDescription: The pull request provider to use when flow.mode is set to "pr". Currently supports GitHub and GitLab.
After finishing a release or hotfix, automatically merge the changes back into the develop branch. This keeps develop up to date with production fixes and releases.
examples: true - Merge back to develop after release/hotfix (default)
false - Do not merge back to develop

detailedDescription: Enable Jira Cloud integration for ticket management and automatic branch-ticket linking. When enabled, Kunj can list tickets, create issues, and automatically link branches to Jira tickets.
Your Jira Cloud instance URL (e.g., https://company.atlassian.net). This is required for API access.
Email address associated with your Jira account. Used for authentication with API token.
API token for authentication. Generate at https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens
Default Jira project key to use when creating tickets (e.g., PROJ, DEV). You can override this when creating tickets.
Default type when creating Jira tickets. Can be overridden with --type flag.
Jira board ID for sprint operations (optional). Used by "kunj jira list --sprint" to show tickets in active sprint. Find this in your board URL.
When enabled, AI will automatically analyze branch commits and generate ticket summaries and descriptions when creating Jira tickets. Requires AI to be enabled.
Enable Slack integration to pull channel activity into team reports. Requires a Slack app with channels:history, channels:read, groups:read, groups:history, and users:read scopes.
Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...) from your Slack app. Found under OAuth & Permissions in your app settings. Requires scopes: channels:history, channels:read, groups:read, groups:history, users:read.
Signing Secret from your Slack app's Basic Information page. Used to verify requests originate from Slack.
App-Level Token (xapp-...) for Socket Mode. Generate under Basic Information → App-Level Tokens with connections:write scope. Optional — only needed for Socket Mode features.
Slack channel IDs to post team reports to. Reports are automatically posted to all listed channels when running "kunj team". Configure via interactive editor for a channel selector.

description: Directory where new worktrees are created
detailedDescription: Supports ${repoconfig} (the .git directory, or the repository itself when bare), ${repoRoot}, ${repoName}, ${home} and ${branch}. Relative paths are resolved from the main repository root. Unless ${branch} appears, the branch directory is appended automatically.

description: Command used by `kunj worktree open` to open a worktree
detailedDescription: The worktree path is appended as the last argument. For VS Code-style editors (code, cursor, codium, windsurf) kunj adds -r to reuse the current window, or -n with --new-window. Set to an empty string to disable opening an editor.
examples: code - Open in Visual Studio Code (default)
code -n - Always open a new VS Code window

description: Command run by the pre-worktree-create hook
detailedDescription: Runs before `kunj worktree add` creates a worktree. A non-zero exit aborts the creation. The command runs through the shell with ${repoRoot}, ${repoconfig}, ${repoName}, ${home}, ${worktree}, ${worktreePath}, ${branch} expanded, and receives KUNJ_HOOK, KUNJ_REPO_ROOT, KUNJ_WORKTREE_PATH, KUNJ_BRANCH in its environment. Edit the config file by hand to list several commands as a JSON array. Executable scripts named pre-worktree-create in ~/.kunj/hooks or ~/.kunj/<repo>/hooks run as well; see `kunj hooks`.

description: Command run by the post-worktree-create hook
detailedDescription: Runs inside a freshly created worktree, after keep files have been copied in (e.g. to install dependencies). The command runs through the shell with ${repoRoot}, ${repoconfig}, ${repoName}, ${home}, ${worktree}, ${worktreePath}, ${branch} expanded, and receives KUNJ_HOOK, KUNJ_REPO_ROOT, KUNJ_WORKTREE_PATH, KUNJ_BRANCH in its environment. description: Container image override (default: the repo's devcontainer, else kunj-sandbox)
Command `kunj container agent` runs inside the container (in tmux)
Host environment variable names forwarded into containers when set; NAME=value entries are passed literally
Host files copied into new containers, as hostPath:containerPath
Copy the repository's keep files into new containers
Egress allowlist of domains; empty means open internet (the host and LAN are always blocked)
Allow containers to reach the Docker host (host.docker.internal)
Docker context used for every docker call
CPU limit passed to docker run (e.g. 2)
Memory limit passed to docker run (e.g. 4g)
Ports always published at container start
`kunj container agent` starts a background `forward --auto` that forwards every new port the container listens on to 127.0.0.1
Container ports `forward --auto` never forwards (ports below 1024 are never forwarded)
`kunj container prune` also removes stopped containers created more than this many days ago (0 = off)
detailedDescription: Off by default. A container removed this way still has to pass the remove guard (no unpushed commits, stashes or uncommitted changes) unless prune is run with --force.

description: Docker inside branch containers: off, sysbox (needs the sysbox-runc runtime on the Docker host) or privileged (needs container.allowPrivileged; refused on Docker Desktop)
detailedDescription: Each container then runs its own dockerd, its /var/lib/docker on a per-branch volume, so docker compose up works inside. The container keeps its capabilities. sysbox keeps inner containers inside the sandbox's user namespace; privileged gives the container root on the Docker host (on a Mac, its VM), so use it only on a dedicated Docker context. Needs the kunj sandbox image (no devcontainer or container.image).

description: Allow container.dockerInDocker "privileged" (root on the Docker host or its VM); it is still refused on Docker Desktop
Sidecar services (Postgres, Redis, ...) started next to each branch container, by name
detailedDescription: An object of name: { image, env?, command?, port?, healthcheck?, volumes?, dependsOn? }; edit the config file by hand. Each service runs on the branch's own network and is reached by its name (postgres:5432). It gets only the env declared here, only named volumes (created per branch), no added capabilities and no published ports. The blueprint's services win over these by name, and these over the devcontainer's compose services.

description: MCP servers on this machine bridged into the container for its Claude Code; only "chrome" (a browser) for now
detailedDescription: An object of name: { command?, args?, env?, allowOrigins? }; edit the config file by hand (host config only, never the blueprint). Off while empty. {"chrome": {}} runs npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --isolated (an empty, isolated browser profile) on this machine when `kunj ct agent` starts, and adds a matching entry to the container user's ~/.claude.json. The server gets only PATH, HOME and its env. allowOrigins (default http://localhost and http://127.0.0.1, any port) limits the URLs navigate_page and new_page may open. One session at a time per server.

description: Command `kunj agent` runs in a host tmux session for a worktree
